title: HECM Servicing Accounting Worksheet: Settlement of a Stopped Draw Check
content:
**Which check.** On a Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM), the stopped draw check handled is the line-of-credit draw that references the loan's most recently created draw request, by its creation timestamp, with disbursement method check and request status withdrawn, handled only while no return entry references that draw. The stopped check's amount is the amount of that draw, and a loan with no such draw has nothing to settle.

**Accrual months charged.** The accrual months charged are the number of calendar months from the month of the stopped check's effective date to the month of the most recent interest accrual posted on the loan, when that accrual is dated after the effective date, and 0 when no interest accrual is dated after it. Interest accruals post once a month, so the most recent one is a single entry.

**Settlement.** The stopped-check settlement is the stopped check's amount plus the interest returned, the premium returned and the compounding returned, rounded half up to the cent once, at the end, where:

- the interest returned is the stopped check's amount multiplied by the interest rate, divided by 100, multiplied by the accrual months charged, divided by 12;
- the premium returned is the stopped check's amount multiplied by the plan's annual mortgage insurance premium rate, divided by 100, multiplied by the premium months, divided by 12.

The interest rate is the loan's note rate, the premium months are the accrual months charged, and the compounding returned is 0.00.

**Worked figure (hypothetical inputs).** A stopped check of 10000.00 effective in March; the most recent interest accrual is dated in July, after the effective date, so the accrual months charged are 4. With a note rate of 6.000 percent and a premium rate of 0.50 percent:

| Line | Amount |
|---|---|
| stopped check's amount | 10000.00 |
| interest returned: 10000.00 multiplied by 6.000, divided by 100, multiplied by 4, divided by 12 | 200.00 |
| premium returned: 10000.00 multiplied by 0.50, divided by 100, multiplied by 4, divided by 12 | 16.666… (unrounded) |
| compounding returned | 0.00 |
| settlement, rounded once | 10216.67 |

Had the most recent interest accrual been dated in March on or before the effective date, the accrual months charged would be 0 and the settlement would be the check's amount alone.
